text.p: Pakistani stocks closed higher on Monday on technical correction after four days of consecutive falls, dealers said.
The Karachi Stock Exchange 100-share index closed 2.90 points, or 0.21 percent, higher at 1,372.40 amid 190 losers and 78 gainers.
The overall market sentiment was bearish but technical correction pulled the index up, dealer Ali Raza said.
"Most of the day's trading was marked by short-covering as the market will remain closed for four days from Wednesday onwards," dealer Salman Ahmad of Finex Securities said.
Financial institutions remained on the sidelines and did not provide any support to the market, one broker said. The market was likely to open mixed on Tuesday.
Adamjee Insurance rose 1.50 rupees to 88.50, Dewan Salman Fibre 1.05 to 28.75, Fauji Fertilizer 1.00 to 68.50, HUBCO 0.25 to 31.95. PTCL fell 0.20 to 26.90 and Parke-Davis 5.00 to 535.
